newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex's Slim says wants funds investigation.
newsitem.headline: Telmex's Slim says wants funds investigation.

text.p: The chairman of Telefonos de Mexico, Carlos Slim Helu, said on Friday that he supported an audit of government accounts to find $1.34 billion from the privatizing of the telephone company that have gone missing.
"I consider it fundamental that we investigate this to the fullest," he told reporters.

Mexican lawmakers said $1.34 billion was missing from the 1990 privatization of the telephone company. They said they found thousands of other anomalies in a public audit of the last year of ex-President Carlos Salinas' government.
"What the (government) Commission must do is investigate how the funds from the privatization were applied," said Slim.

The Mexican press denounced the missing cash in banner headlines and speculated that officials may have carried on a murky tradition in 1994 of stuffing pockets with public funds just before the president's six-year-term came to a close.
But the congressmen who pointed out the anomalies also said the money may have been misplaced due to accounting errors and could show up eventually as other audits were carried out.
The committee issued a report on Thursday after auditing only 10 percent of 1994 public accounts that found 3,089 irregularities in 552 cases.

The congressmen held out hope the missing funds would be accounted for by the time they finish their audit in 45 days. Slim also told reporters that Telmex was ready for the competition that will start in the Mexican telephone sector next year.
"We are used to living in a world of competitive business," he said.
